input.title: BH | Premier Damme Acacia Console Table — In Espresso
input.descriptionHtml:
Damme, a small town on the old canal outside Bruges, is known today as a book village, and its brick houses hold secondhand bookshops where a whole afternoon goes to browsing and the finds come home in a bag. This console table is made for a house of readers. At 78 inches long it gives a row of books, a reading lamp and the week's finds a long place to rest, right where you pass by on the way to a chair.

It is made of acacia with a richly worked finish that has real depth, and its narrow 16-inch depth keeps it close to the wall in a hall or behind a sofa. The long, clean top is the main event, with nothing fussy to get in the way of what you set on it. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it behind a sofa that faces into the room or along a hall wall, with stacked books, a pair of lamps, a bowl for keys and a plant at one end. This listing is for one console table.

input.title: BH | Premier Madeleine Shagreen Console Table
input.descriptionHtml:
A Saturday on the Place de la Madeleine means a slow tour of the fine food shops: chocolates from one, a tin of tea from another, a bottle chosen for that evening. This console is made for setting it all out once you are home. Its long, slim top holds a tray of treats and a bottle with its glasses while guests arrive, and its shagreen-grained leather, the pebbled finish Paris has loved since the eighteenth century, dresses it for the occasion.

Its frame is iron, and brass hardware adds a warm, bright note against the leather. At only 14 inches deep it fits a hall or the wall behind a sofa without crowding either, and it arrives fully assembled.

Place it in a dining room as a serving table with a cake stand, the coffee cups and a box of chocolates, or in a hall with a lamp, a bowl for keys and a stack of art books beside a pair of candlesticks. This listing is for one console table.

input.descriptionHtml:
Every Paris apartment has its spot by the door where the day starts and ends: keys dropped, the mail sorted, a glance in the mirror on the way out. This console is made for that spot. Its three drawers take the things that would otherwise pile up on top, and its shagreen-embossed leather gives the spot by the door a quiet polish.

The wood case is wrapped in that embossed leather, and each drawer is lined with a patterned paper, a detail you only discover when you open one. At 64 inches long and just 18 deep, it gives a long run of surface without stepping far into a hallway, and it arrives fully assembled.

Keep it by the front door under a mirror, holding a lamp and a small bowl that catches the keys, or behind a sofa with books stacked at one end and a vase of flowers at the other. In a dining room it holds candles on top and folded napkins below, ready for the table. This listing is for one console table.

input.title: BH | Premier Dufftown Marble Console Table — In Espresso with White Marble Top
input.descriptionHtml:
In a whisky town like Dufftown a good bottle is meant to be shared, so it makes sense to keep a few on show, ready to pour for whoever calls in at the end of the day. This console table is made to hold that small home bar. Its long marble top gives the bottles, a decanter and a row of glasses a cool, solid surface, and at nearly seven feet long it leaves room for a lamp at each end.

The top is white marble over a base of acacia, raised on turned legs, and it is only 14 inches deep, so it stands close behind a sofa or along a hall without taking over the room. At 170 lbs it is steady under a full tray. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Use it behind a sofa or along a dining room wall with a tray of glasses, a decanter and a water jug, or in a wide entry hall with lamps, a bowl for keys and framed photographs. This listing is for one console table.

input.title: BH | Premier Saint-Rémy Pine Console Table
input.descriptionHtml:
On market mornings in Saint-Rémy, below the hills of the Alpilles, people walk home under the plane trees with baskets of melons, goat's cheese and bunches of herbs, and everything lands on the long table by the door before it finds its place. This console is made to take that whole basket. At nearly eight feet long its top takes the shopping, a lamp and a jug of flowers all at once, and its three drawers hold the market bags, napkins and candles.

It is built from reclaimed pine and given a gentle distressing that softens its edges and gives it the look of a piece that has stood in a farmhouse hall for years. At 36 inches tall it stands a little higher than many consoles, a comfortable height for unpacking or arranging flowers without bending. It arrives fully assembled.

Give it a long wall in an entry or hallway with a pair of lamps and a big bowl of fruit, or set it behind a large sofa with books and a jug of olive branches. This listing is for one console table.

input.title: BH | Premier Fjällbacka Reclaimed Pine Console Table — In Cocoa
input.descriptionHtml:
Coming home to a summer house in Fjällbacka means a hall full of sandals, sun hats and fishing lines, and somewhere to drop the keys before heading straight back out to the rocks. This console table is made for that busy doorway. Its long, narrow top holds the things you reach for on the way out, and at only 13 inches deep it sits close to the wall without crowding the path to the door.

It is reclaimed pine, worked into a clean geometric form that borrows the solid, honest lines of Brutalist building, and the timber's history shows in its grain and surface. More than five feet long, it gives a hall or the back of a sofa a generous run of display space. It arrives fully assembled.

Stand it in a dining room to hold the decanter, glasses and a pair of candlesticks, or in a narrow hall with a small lamp, a dish for keys and a framed print leaning against the wall. This listing is for one console table.

input.title: BH | Premier Montélimar Carved Pine Console Table — In Cocoa
input.descriptionHtml:
Montélimar, in the Drôme, has made nougat from honey and almonds for centuries, and the town is still full of shops setting it out in great slabs to be cut and shared. This console is made for setting things out in the same generous way: a tray of glasses before guests arrive, a bowl of fruit, a lamp and the mail. Its carved apron, the rail under the top, is worked in a pattern of six-sided cells and crosses that nods to the honey at the heart of the town's famous sweet.

The table is pine, and the carved apron sits level with the edge of the top, so the front reads as one clean face rather than a top resting on a frame. At only 16 inches deep it fits a hallway or the back of a sofa, and at 51 lbs it is light to place. It ships in one box and needs assembly.

Use it in an entry with a lamp, a dish for keys and a framed print above, or behind a sofa with a pair of candlesticks and the books you are working through. This listing is for one console table.

Put it behind a sofa in a living room or library with two reading lamps, a row of hardbacks between bookends and a small bowl for reading glasses, or along a long hall wall. This listing is for one console table.

input.title: BH | Premier Saint-Émilion Pine Half-Moon Console Table — In Driftwood
input.descriptionHtml:
In Saint-Émilion the lanes are steep and narrow, and the hall of an old house is often just wide enough for one small table: somewhere to drop the keys, leave the mail and set down the bottle you are bringing to a friend's supper. This half-moon console is made for that kind of hall. Its rounded front leaves room to pass on the way out the door, and its straight back sits neatly against the wall.

It is made of pine in a worn finish, in the shape the French call a demilune, a table with a straight back and a curved front. At 44 inches wide and 18 deep it fits places where a full-length console would crowd the room, from an entry to a landing to the space between two windows. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it inside the front door with a lamp, a small dish for keys and a mirror above, or between two windows in a dining room for candles and a decanter. This listing is for one console table.

input.descriptionHtml:
In Verona the opera starts late, so the hour before belongs to getting ready: a drink poured at home, a last look in the mirror, and keys and tickets left by the door where nobody can forget them. This console table is made for that moment on the way out. Its marble top is just 12 inches deep, so it fits a slim entry, and its iron frame rises up around the edges of the stone, framing it neatly.

The top is white marble held in an iron frame finished in aged nickel, with the legs carried up past the stone to enclose it. At 30 inches high it sits comfortably behind a sofa backed against a window, and at three feet wide it suits a small apartment hall as well as a larger room. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Put it in the entry with a tray for keys, a small lamp and a mirror above, or behind a sofa with a pair of candlesticks and a bowl of lemons. This listing is for one console table.

input.descriptionHtml:
A long Carrara lunch needs somewhere for things to wait: the bread, a bottle opened to breathe, the platter that comes back for a second round. In a town that has quarried marble since Roman times, that place is usually a slab of stone. This console table brings that cool, ready surface into the house. Its marble top runs nearly five feet along a wall, and at only 14 inches deep it stands close against it, clear of chairs and passing guests.

The marble is white with a lightly distressed face, softening its edges into the look of old stone, and it rests on a frame of iron wrought by hand in a dark, rustic finish. The open frame keeps the piece light to the eye for all its 136 lbs. It comes in two boxes and needs assembly.

Use it in a dining room as a serving table, with a pair of lamps, a bowl of lemons and the dishes waiting their turn, or behind a sofa, or in an entry hall under a mirror with a tray for keys and the mail. This listing is for one console table.

A Danish house by the sea at Klampenborg is planned around light and around guests, and the hall is where an afternoon visit begins: coats off, a greeting, the coffee already on. This console table is made for that first moment inside the door. Its long top gives keys, the mail and a bowl of something seasonal a calm place to land, and its smooth, curving lines carry the quiet modern feel of a bright Danish room.

It is made of wood, close to six feet long and only 19 inches deep, so it fits along a hall or behind a sofa without crowding the way through. Its 180 lbs give it a steady footing, and the curves that shape it are finished so they feel smooth under the hand.

Stand it against the wall of an entry with a lamp and a mirror above, or behind a sofa that floats in the room, with books, a pair of candlesticks and a vase of cut branches along the top. This listing is for one console table.

In Rothenburg ob der Tauber the old trades still announce themselves above the doors, in wrought-iron signs hammered and scrolled by hand, so a visitor knows the baker's from the smith's before stepping inside. This console table is made for the moment you come home and set things down. Its frame is shaped by hand at the forge, and its glass top lets the ironwork show from every side while it holds the keys, the mail and a lamp.

The frame is solid iron bar, worked by hand and chased, meaning patterned with a tool, with fine ridges running the full length of every face. Where the bars meet, the corners come together in a three-pointed joint that shows the smith's skill. It is five feet long and 16 inches deep, and it arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Set it in an entry hall with a lamp, a bowl for keys and a mirror above, or stand it behind a sofa with a stack of art books and a single tall vase of branches. This listing is for one console table.

Its four small drawers keep sunglasses, keys and loose change sorted, its lower shelf takes baskets and shoes, and at only 12 inches deep it leaves the doorway clear for everyone coming in and going out.

It is made of wood with a warm grain, and its drawers are fitted with aged bronze knobs that are easy to catch on the way past. At five feet long it suits an entrance hall or the back of a sofa. It arrives fully assembled.

Stand it inside the front door with a bowl for keys, a lamp and a mirror above, the shelf below holding a basket of beach towels, or bring it into a dining room to hold napkins and candles. This listing is for one console table.

Set it in an entry hall with a lamp, a bowl of sea glass and a basket for flip-flops, or behind a sofa with family photographs and the summer's beach reads. This listing is for one console table.

The bureau plat, the flat-topped writing table of eighteenth-century Paris, was an open piece with a leather top, made for letters, accounts and the quiet work of running a house. This desk keeps that idea, with a leather surface made for working on. It gives you a broad, smooth surface for a laptop, a notebook and a cup of coffee, and it is just as happy pulled away from the wall and laid for a small dinner.

The case is wood, covered in leather embossed with the pebbled grain of shagreen, so the surface stays warm and soft under the wrists through a long morning of work. At 48 inches wide and 24 deep it holds a computer and a spread of papers side by side without taking over the room, and its 30-inch height suits a standard desk chair or a dining chair. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it beneath a window in a study or a spare bedroom with a lamp, a tray for pens and a few letters waiting for replies, or use it in a small dining nook as a table for two, set with candles and a bottle of wine. This listing is for one desk.

input.title: BH | Premier Quai Voltaire Shagreen Desk — In Charcoal with Brass Frame
input.descriptionHtml:
On the Quai Voltaire, the green bookstalls of the bouquinistes line the river wall across from the antique dealers, and the whole quay feels made for people who write: letters, notes, the list made before the day begins. This desk is made for that daily hour at the page. Its top is leather pressed with the pebbled grain of shagreen, warm and quiet under your wrists, and three drawers keep the pens, the good paper and the unanswered letters close by.

The leather top rests on iron with a brass-toned finish, a clean, modern outline that keeps the desk looking light in a room. Each drawer is lined with marbleized paper, the swirled paper of old bookbinding, so even the inside is a pleasure to open. It arrives fully assembled.

Give it the light from a window in a study, or a quiet corner of the bedroom, with a lamp, a cup of pens and a notebook open to the day's list, or set it behind a sofa, where it serves as a console table on the days it is not a desk. This listing is for one desk.

input.title: BH | Premier Girona Iron and Wood Desk — In Chestnut with Jet Base
input.descriptionHtml:
Girona's old quarter has been a place of study since the Middle Ages, when scholars worked in the narrow streets of the Call, the medieval Jewish quarter, and writing there still feels like something done at a solid table by a deep window. This desk is made for those long sessions at the page. Its top runs 37 inches deep, room to spread out books, a laptop and notes side by side, and its drawer storage keeps the pens and papers close.

The top is old wood in a pale, bleached finish, set on a dark metal frame with iron detailing, and the two together give it the feel of a piece that has worked hard for years. It ships in two boxes and needs assembly.

Put it in a study or library under a window, with a desk lamp, a stack of reference books and a jar of pencils, and a comfortable chair pulled up for a long afternoon of writing. This listing is for one desk.

input.title: BH | Premier Shanagarry Reclaimed Fir Kitchen Desk
input.descriptionHtml:
At Ballymaloe, the cookery school in Shanagarry, County Cork, a good meal starts on paper: the menu written out, the list made, the recipe read through before anyone picks up a knife. This desk is made for that same work in your own kitchen. It gives the shopping list, the recipe cards and the cookbooks a proper place of their own, and its three drawers keep pens, notebooks and the takeout menus out of sight until they are needed.

It is reclaimed fir, timber that has had a working life before, so its surface already carries marks of age. At 51 inches wide and 22 deep there is room for an open cookbook, a laptop and a cup of tea side by side, and at 32 inches high it sits comfortably with a standard chair. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a corner of the kitchen under a window, with a jar of pens, a stand for the cookbook and a pinboard of recipes above, or use it in a hall for the household bills and mail. This listing is for one desk.

input.title: BH | Premier Chawton Pine Writing Desk — In Stone
input.descriptionHtml:
At Chawton, Jane Austen wrote in the family's shared drawing room on small sheets of paper she could slip out of sight, and a creaking door warned her when someone was coming. This desk is made for that kind of everyday writing, at home and in the middle of family life. It is compact enough for a living room corner or a landing, yet its pair of drawers and the two doors beside them put letters, bills and the laptop tidily out of view when the work is done.

It is made of pine, and each of the two doors and two drawers carries a raised panel, a panel that stands proud of its frame, with a scalloped edge that softens the whole front. At 53 inches wide it gives room for a lamp, a notebook and a cup of tea. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it under a window in a bedroom or living room with a lamp, a jar of pens and a framed print, a side chair pulled up and the stationery stored below. This listing is for one desk.

Sir Walter Scott wrote many of his later novels in the study at Abbotsford, the house he built beside the River Tweed, surrounded by his books. This desk is made for that kind of daily, focused work. Its leather top is a warm, quiet surface to write on, and its drawers keep pens, notebooks and letters close at hand, so the work stays on the desk and the clutter stays out of sight.

The top is leather with an aged look, set on a base of iron bars with a hammered, worn finish. The drawers have cast brass pulls in the campaign style, the squared handles first used on travelling chests, and inside they are lined with embossed handmade paper. At 49 inches wide it suits a study or the corner of a bedroom. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it under a window in a study or library with a desk lamp, a stack of notebooks and a cup of coffee, and a good chair pulled up. This listing is for one desk.

The cabinetmakers of the Faubourg Saint-Antoine made writing furniture for people with a great deal to keep: letters, ledgers, seals and the good paper, all within reach of the chair. This long writing cabinet is made for keeping things in that same good order. It is covered in shagreen, the pebbled finish the French still call galuchat, and inside it opens to a natural teak interior with lined drawers, so the everyday clutter of a desk finally has a proper home.

The lined drawers come in two depths, shallow ones for pens, stationery and chargers and deeper ones for notebooks and files, and a large interior compartment takes boxes, albums and the things you only need now and then. It stands eight inches clear of the floor, which keeps it light in the room and makes cleaning underneath easy, and accents in a gold finish catch the lamplight. At seven feet long it reads as one calm line along a wall.

Run it along the wall of a study or home office with a lamp and a framed print above, or use it in a living room for photo albums and games, with a pair of bowls on top. This listing is for one writing cabinet.

input.title: BH | Premier Fitzrovia Large Herringbone Jupe Dining Table
input.descriptionHtml:
In 1835 a London cabinetmaker named Robert Jupe patented a round dining table that could grow: its top parted outward and extra leaves filled the gaps, so the table was always the right size for whoever came to dinner. This table is made for the evenings when the guest list keeps growing. It opens from a generous round to a far larger one, its leaves store inside the table itself, and the herringbone pattern laid into its oak top makes it the centre of the room open or closed.

The top is quarter-sawn oak veneer, a cut that shows a straight, even grain, and the whole table stands on a single faceted octagonal pedestal, so there are no corner legs in the way however many chairs are pulled up. The extension runs on an aluminum mechanism built for smooth, easy opening. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Give it the middle of the dining room under a pendant light: closed for a weeknight supper, opened out for a holiday meal with every seat filled and the serving dishes passed around. This listing is for one large dining table.

input.descriptionHtml:
The expanding round table patented in London in 1835 solved a problem every host still knows: four are invited, six turn up, and nobody wants to be squeezed in at a corner. This medium table is made for exactly those evenings. Closed, it is a comfortable round for a small supper; opened, it grows to 71 inches across, and its leaves tuck away inside the table itself, so they are always within reach when the doorbell rings again.

The top is oak laid in herringbone marquetry, small pieces of wood set in a zigzag pattern, and it rests on an eight-sided pedestal with curved facets, so chairs can be drawn up anywhere around the edge. Its aluminum mechanism lets the top part and close with an easy, even pull. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Hang a pendant light over it in a dining room or a large kitchen and keep a bowl of fruit at its centre on ordinary nights, then add the leaves and pull up extra chairs when friends arrive with a second bottle. This listing is for one medium dining table.

Its aluminum mechanism lets the top part and close with an easy, even pull. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

In the 1720s Lord Burlington built Chiswick House as a villa for entertaining, and the Georgian houses that grew up around it kept the habit: dinner for four, then six, and whoever else could be fitted in. This round table is made for that kind of hospitality. Closed, it is a neat round for a small supper, and when more guests are coming it opens to seat six, with everyone still facing the centre and no one left at a corner.

It is a Jupe table, a round table whose top divides and slides apart so leaves can drop in between, and the leaves live inside the table when not in use. It opens on an extruded aluminum mechanism made for smooth, easy opening. The veneered top is laid in a sunburst, its grain radiating from the centre, and it stands on a faceted pedestal built from many panels and finished with a brass-capped foot. It arrives in two boxes and needs assembly.

Place it in a dining room or a sunroom under a pendant with a bowl of fruit at its heart, and draw it open the night six are coming for a birthday dinner, with candles and the good china out. This listing is for one dining table.
